npc.name: Matron Velia
npc.description: A silver-braided human administrator who knows every family debt and every road song.
npc.dialogue: The Marches are not empty wilderness. Every hill has a name, and every name has someone ready to fight for it.

npc.name: Captain Orran Vale
npc.description: A scarred half-orc officer whose patience is more intimidating than his axe.
npc.dialogue: Trouble moves like weather. Watch the roads and you can see the storm forming.

npc.name: Tamsin Quickcart
npc.description: A halfling peddler with bright scarves, louder opinions, and suspiciously useful maps.
npc.dialogue: Buy now. Regret later. Or regret now and buy later; both end at my cart.

npc.name: Quartermaster Bren
npc.description: A practical dwarf with ink-black fingers and no tolerance for heroic under-planning.
npc.dialogue: Heroes die when they forget rope. Buy rope.

npc.name: Scribe Miravel
npc.description: An elven records officer who annotates gossip as if it might become law.
npc.dialogue: Rumor is not evidence, but it is often evidence wearing a cheaper cloak.

npc.name: Prior Annel
npc.description: A calm cleric who can bless a blade, scold a noble, and comfort a stranger in the same breath.
npc.dialogue: Mercy is not softness. It is discipline with a lantern.

npc.name: Seer Liora
npc.description: A blind aasimar seer whose white eyes follow invisible constellations.
npc.dialogue: The dead star is patient. That is why we must not be.

npc.name: Dockmaster Keel
npc.description: A dragonborn customs master who remembers every crate, captain, and bribe offered at the river gate.
npc.dialogue: Declare your cargo honestly. I can smell lies and lamp oil from across the bridge.

npc.name: Marla Hen-and-Bell
npc.description: A broad-shouldered innkeeper who hosts travelers, informants, and at least one disguised noble per month.
npc.dialogue: Eat first, talk second. Hungry people make bad bargains.

npc.name: Kael Thorne
npc.description: A young veteran with a dented shield, dry humor, and a fear of becoming the kind of soldier he once followed.
npc.dialogue: I can hold a doorway. I am less good at holding my tongue.

npc.name: Nessa Valequill
npc.description: A tiefling scholar who treats danger as field research and apologizes only when the experiment is over.
npc.dialogue: That rune is either a warning or a recipe. Possibly both.

npc.name: Jailer Pike
npc.description: A tired old guard who has heard every excuse except an original one.
npc.dialogue: Pay the fine, sleep it off, or convince me the goat started it.

npc.name: Ollis Reed
npc.description: A reed-thin boatman who knows Greenbarrow crossings and resents being blamed for Tidebound League ticket policy.
npc.dialogue: I can pole you upriver, but I cannot sell a Terrecester ticket from a locked Hearthwatch window.

npc.name: Pip Thornbarrow
npc.description: A cheerful halfling pathwarden with muddy boots, a sling, and a flawless memory for who owes whom a casserole.
npc.dialogue: Mind the stile, praise the stew, and do not call a burrow house a hole unless you enjoy lectures.

npc.name: Elder Merrian Applebloom
npc.description: A silver-haired halfling matriarch whose soft voice can quiet a market, a militia, or a noble envoy.
npc.dialogue: Applewallow has survived lords, floods, owlbears, and three winters of turnip soup. We will survive this too, but not by being careless.

npc.name: Hob Tumblepot
npc.description: A broad-smiling co-op keeper who treats inventory as sacred community memory.
npc.dialogue: A shared pantry is a promise. Someone is trying to turn it into a weapon.

npc.name: Tressa Goodfurrow
npc.description: A sharp-eyed halfling scout with burrs in her cloak, a shortbow across her back, and no patience for heroic stomping.
npc.dialogue: The ground has tells. Right now it is telling me something under it has a plan.

npc.name: Seed-Warden Ysella
npc.description: A translucent halfling seed-warden bound to the first cache, equal parts grandmother, guardian, and hearthfire.
npc.dialogue: Fallowmaw calls hunger order. We call sharing survival. Choose which law leaves this burrow.

npc.name: Ysella Seedwake
npc.description: A warm-eyed ancestral spirit who keeps the First Seed Cache from those who would own what was meant to be shared.
npc.dialogue: The path through the loam is simple if you remember the first oath: bowl, hand, loaf, seed.

npc.name: Aunt Mara Puddlepot
npc.description: A flour-dusted kitchen commander who knows every family allergy, feud, and courtship in Applewallow.
npc.dialogue: Soup first. Questions after. Panic never improved a broth.

npc.name: Fenlo Twicebarrel
npc.description: A red-cheeked cider maker who judges character by how a person treats borrowed cups.
npc.dialogue: Best cider in the Marches. Worst time for the earth to start chewing wagons.

npc.name: Lina Honeybell
npc.description: A calm beekeeper with veiled hair, wax-stained fingers, and prophetic confidence in her hives.
npc.dialogue: The bees are spelling trouble in circles. That is never decorative.

npc.name: Sister Benna Seedwake
npc.description: A practical priest of Yondalla’s Table who blesses bread knives, birth rooms, scarecrows, and militia spears with equal seriousness.
npc.dialogue: The dead do not mind visitors. They mind thieves.

npc.name: Obo Stoutbarrel
npc.description: A compact militia quartermaster who can arm a dozen farmers from one cupboard and a grudge.
npc.dialogue: Take a sling. Tallfolk always underestimate slings until gravity explains them.

npc.name: Jory Whistlegrain
npc.description: A wiry miller who whistles to the waterwheel and swears it answers in squeaks.
npc.dialogue: The mill knows honest mud. This mud is lying.

npc.name: Old Tobin Manykeys
npc.description: An elderly locksmith who remembers which burrow doors connect, which should not, and which are pretending.
npc.dialogue: A good door keeps out weather, taxmen, and bad manners. Monsters require additional hinges.

npc.name: Kite Underhill
npc.description: A small halfling child with scraped knees, enormous confidence, and a missing pie tin of supposedly legendary importance.
npc.dialogue: Adventurers get shields. I had a pie tin. Then the tunnel took it.

npc.name: Dorrick Pennymeasure
npc.description: A gnome antiquarian attempting to study Freehold burial customs without being exiled by offended grandmothers.
npc.dialogue: For the record, I now understand that asking to borrow ancestral mud is not a neutral phrase.

npc.name: Nessa Hollowheel
npc.description: A half-elf cartwright repairing wagon wheels while mediating between outside merchants and local field law.
npc.dialogue: The Freeholds are generous, not naïve. There is a very expensive difference.

npc.name: Khorra Ironmile
npc.description: A broad-shouldered dwarf cartographer with chalked boots, survey chains, and a professional hatred of anyone who calls the free road unclaimed.
npc.dialogue: Roads are promises laid in stone. Someone is breaking ours cart by cart.

npc.name: Foreman Dorrak Falduhr
npc.description: The working head of Bhon Falduhr, more comfortable reading ore than politics, but impossible to intimidate where worker safety is concerned.
npc.dialogue: Sun-iron comes out of this mountain by paid hands and living backs. Nobody takes those hands from me.

npc.name: Nalda Brightvein
npc.description: A meticulous dwarf assayer whose spectacles have six rotating lenses and whose patience has none.
npc.dialogue: The numbers are clean, which means the theft is dirty somewhere else.

npc.name: Rusk Flintwake
npc.description: A one-eyed hill scout who reads broken axles and boot scuffs with the delicacy of a court poet.
npc.dialogue: Bandits steal coin. These raiders stole ore, manifests, and people-shaped measurements.

npc.name: Hadrin of the Lost Shift
npc.description: The ghost of a miner whose crew sealed the Quiet Tunnels rather than let a tyrant inherit their work.
npc.dialogue: We held the dark with picks and lunch pails. You have sharper tools. Use them well.

npc.name: Helka Seven-Rivets
npc.description: A dwarf roadwarden whose armor is repaired with seven visible rivets, each commemorating a different caravan she brought home.
npc.dialogue: If the signals fail, the road becomes six isolated graves with wheels.

npc.name: Karvi Chainclock
npc.description: A clockwork-handed caravan master who schedules wagons with mathematical severity and curses raiders with artistic freedom.
npc.dialogue: My wagons can outrun weather, debt, and bad cooking. They cannot outrun insider knowledge.

npc.name: Bera Copperpulse
npc.description: A dwarf medic treating injuries caused by cold magic, phantom picks, and fear.
npc.dialogue: A cut tells you what blade made it. These wounds tell me someone is practicing on workers.

npc.name: Nalda Brightvein
npc.description: Nalda can identify a sun-iron seam by smell, color, and the mood of the crucible flame.
npc.dialogue: Bring me a true sample from the face, and I can shame every counterfeit in Vandarom.

npc.name: Sella Quickgear
npc.description: A gnome engineer adopted into three dwarf crews after saving a lift full of miners with a bootlace and profanity.
npc.dialogue: Somebody forced the side gate from below. If that lift drops, the mountain gets a vote.

npc.name: Ulfra Stonepsalm
npc.description: A gray-bearded dwarf who keeps the shift rolls, funeral songs, and unpaid jokes of miners who did not return.
npc.dialogue: Names are wages paid to the dead. Bring me the tally stone and I will pay what is owed.

npc.name: Orris Vale
npc.description: A human broker trying to keep neutral trade alive while every faction accuses every other faction of theft.
npc.dialogue: I move goods, not allegiances. Someone is using my schedules like a knife.

npc.name: Tali Emberpot
npc.description: A halfling cook whose stew line hears more reliable intelligence than most spy networks.
npc.dialogue: People confess over stew. Mostly about salt, sometimes about murder.

npc.name: Guildspeaker Brunda Vandar
npc.description: The elected speaker of Vandarom, chosen by guild vote and known for ending council arguments by handing everyone a hammer and a problem.
npc.dialogue: We sell to factions. We do not belong to them. The Cabal will learn the difference.

npc.name: Iolanthe Reedglass
npc.description: An elf advocate who audits foreign contracts to make sure Dawnhammer neutrality is not abused.
npc.dialogue: Neutrality is not naivety. Every buyer leaves a shadow in the paperwork.

npc.name: Rogan Anvilwake
npc.description: A master smith whose hands are scarred by honest heat and whose temper rises at counterfeit marks.
npc.dialogue: A forged maker mark is not fraud. It is identity theft with casualties.

npc.name: Maerin Brassbuckle
npc.description: A cheerful dwarf merchant selling mine gear, sun-iron tools, and unsolicited advice about tunnel footwear.
npc.dialogue: Buy quality once or cheap twice, assuming the cheap version lets you survive the first lesson.

npc.name: Jassa Oxfriend
npc.description: A half-orc quartermaster who knows every ox by name and every suspicious buyer by smell.
npc.dialogue: Supplies move when paperwork, hooves, and nerves all agree. Lately only the hooves are honest.

npc.name: Torva Runehand
npc.description: A nonbinary dwarf loremason who treats maker marks as sacred signatures rather than decoration.
npc.dialogue: The press remembers every mark. This bone tried to make it lie.

npc.name: Gimla Openmug
npc.description: A retired shield-smith who now protects workers by making sure grievances are heard before they become riots.
npc.dialogue: My taproom has three rules: pay your tab, name your complaint, and no one owns another person's hands.

npc.name: Mara Chain-Sunder
npc.description: A wounded dwarf smith who escaped the first capture team and hid long enough to learn the Cabal's production plan.
npc.dialogue: They measured us for shackles before they measured the forge beds. Break the pens first.

npc.name: Lieutenant Sera Duskshield
npc.description: A calm shield-dwarf lieutenant who rotates patrols through every district and knows which streets go quiet before trouble.
npc.dialogue: A hub survives on boring discipline. Boring discipline is what lets heroes chase the dramatic fires.

npc.name: Sergeant Vell Ardent
npc.description: A human veteran with a cedar practice sword and a voice that can stop a tavern brawl through two walls.
npc.dialogue: Hold the line, mind your flanks, and never trust a clean pair of boots.

npc.name: Constable Brindle Tallow
npc.description: A stout halfling constable who settles neighbor disputes, missing chickens, and actual conspiracies with the same notebook.
npc.dialogue: People call it gossip until it saves a patrol.

npc.name: Osrik Bellfounder
npc.description: An elderly dwarf artisan whose family cast the keep bell and every shrine bell in the district. He hears cracks like other people hear lies.
npc.dialogue: A bell remembers the hand that made it. This one remembers something older.

npc.name: Elder Bramblewick Fen
npc.description: A green-coated halfling elder from Applewallow, visiting Hearthwatch to demand that the town protect people before relics.
npc.dialogue: Greenbarrow feeds half your road patrols. Remember that before you call our fields quaint.

npc.name: Lady Isolde Aurelian
npc.description: A poised noblewoman whose house funded the keep generations ago and now hides fear behind impeccable manners.
npc.dialogue: The city must see confidence, even if confidence must be tailored overnight.

npc.name: Varo Silk
npc.description: A half-elf courtier who sells secrets to prevent worse secrets from winning.
npc.dialogue: Everyone has a price. The trick is learning whether they want coin, mercy, or silence.

npc.name: Majordomo Renic Vale
npc.description: A tireless tiefling steward who knows exactly which heirlooms are missing and who was last alone with them.
npc.dialogue: Servants do not vanish. They are made invisible by those who benefit.

npc.name: Marketmaster Senna Brisk
npc.description: A quick-talking human marketmaster who can identify a forged tax seal by smell and a desperate merchant by posture.
npc.dialogue: Trade is a bloodstream. Poison it and the whole Marches go cold.

npc.name: Fex Coppergrin
npc.description: A cheerful goblin artificer whose “mostly safe” gear is usually safer than his explanations.
npc.dialogue: Good news: it works. Bad news: we learn what it works on together.

npc.name: Guild Notary Pavel
npc.description: A severe aasimar clerk who treats false weights as moral injuries.
npc.dialogue: Ink does not lie. People lie near ink.

npc.name: Forewoman Naia Keelhand
npc.description: A broad-shouldered goliath forewoman who runs the quay crews and has no patience for smugglers who endanger dockhands.
npc.dialogue: You can hide a crate. You cannot hide the people hurt by it.

npc.name: River-Priest Calan
npc.description: A sea-elf priest who blesses barges, names the drowned, and speaks to the river when it refuses ordinary maps.
npc.dialogue: Water keeps accounts longer than kings.

npc.name: Initiate Pella
npc.description: A young gnome acolyte juggling charity ledgers, candle tithes, and a very opinionated temple cat.
npc.dialogue: Faith is logistics with a soul.

npc.name: Sister Mara Hush
npc.description: A half-orc healer whose gentleness never prevents her from physically removing fools from the infirmary.
npc.dialogue: Sit down before you fall down. That is both medical advice and theology.

npc.name: Archmage Caldus Vane
npc.description: A raven-haired elf mage whose expensive composure frays whenever the dead star shifts by a fraction of a degree.
npc.dialogue: The star is not above us. It is aimed at us.

npc.name: Envoy Thalen Moonscript
npc.description: A moon elf diplomat trying to keep nobles, priests, and mages from starting a jurisdictional war during an actual apocalypse.
npc.dialogue: Jurisdiction is what powerful people argue about while frightened people wait.

npc.name: Apprentice Nyx Emberquill
npc.description: A soot-smudged tiefling apprentice who sells scrolls, collects anomalies, and grins whenever an experiment only nearly explodes.
npc.dialogue: Do not lick the blue residue. That rule is from experience.

npc.name: Archivist Izzet of Nine Keys
npc.description: A meticulous kobold archivist who files forbidden knowledge by danger, language, and bite risk.
npc.dialogue: Some books bite figuratively. Mine are labeled when they bite literally.

npc.name: Pip Mossmantle
npc.description: A moss-haired satyr courier with inked hooves and a perfect memory for safe paths, insulting etiquette, and edible flowers.
npc.dialogue: Do not ask whether the trees are alive. Ask whether they are in a forgiving mood.

npc.name: Rill-of-Silverflies
npc.description: A palm-sized sprite followed by silver fireflies that arrange themselves into warning signs when Rill is too impatient to explain.
npc.dialogue: Messages move fastest when they are frightened. I prefer them merely nervous.

npc.name: Nettle-Veil Herald
npc.description: A masked eladrin herald whose cloak is embroidered with living nettles and diplomatic loopholes.
npc.dialogue: Guests receive hospitality. Trespassers receive lessons. Declare which one you intend to be.

npc.name: Archduchess Thyralune of the White Thorn
npc.description: A luminous archfey noble with antler-like branches crowned in white blossoms. Her grace is real, but so is the city’s fear of her political memory.
npc.dialogue: The Thorn Court remembers beautifully and forgets strategically. The Oracle is what happens when forgetting becomes a crime.

npc.name: Sir Bramble-of-the-Third-Root
npc.description: A beetle-armored knight barely taller than a halfling, formal to the point of absurdity and deadly with a thorn-lance.
npc.dialogue: A vow is armor. Broken, it cuts the wearer first.

npc.name: Elowen Glassroot
npc.description: A dryad archivist grown through a desk of green crystal, patient with scholarship and ruthless with omissions.
npc.dialogue: Bring me facts, not comfort. Comfort is how courts teach history to limp.

npc.name: Keeper Asterion Vale
npc.description: A half-elf astronomer whose eyes reflect moving constellations after too many years guarding a broken Fey mechanism.
npc.dialogue: The Orrery does not predict the dead star. It remembers why the dead star can find us.

npc.name: Vessa Candlecap
npc.description: A cheerful myconid-adopted gnome who sells spore salves, mushroom lanterns, and brutally honest advice.
npc.dialogue: All cures are negotiations. Some are just with your liver.

npc.name: Lorien Witherbloom
npc.description: A changeling tailor who stitches emotions into thorn-silk and refuses to sell black without asking why.
npc.dialogue: A cloak can hide you from guards. Better cloth hides you from stories.

npc.name: Granny Elmoria
npc.description: An elderly awakened elm spirit in an apron, known for spiced tea, severe hospitality, and curses that mostly improve manners.
npc.dialogue: Sit. Eat. Then tell me which disaster has followed you home.

npc.name: Orren Mossmead
npc.description: A halfling beekeeper from Applewallow who married into Onfadell’s orbit and now keeps bees that pollinate spells.
npc.dialogue: Fey honey is like politics: sweet, sticky, and likely to outlive you.

npc.name: Ilex Nine-Songs
npc.description: An androgynous eladrin bard whose harp remembers eight songs they have forgotten and one they are afraid to sing.
npc.dialogue: The ninth song belongs to someone who was made nameless. I would rather learn it before it learns me.

npc.name: Nemae the Name-Witness
npc.description: A veiled Fey witness who records names on their own shadow so even magic cannot erase them twice.
npc.dialogue: Justice without names becomes weather. It destroys whoever stands outside.

npc.name: The Last Named Witness
npc.description: A wounded Concord witness preserved in a ring of mushrooms, able to confirm the Oracle’s relic is part of the Astral Crown ward-chain.
npc.dialogue: She was wronged. She is also wrong. Both truths must survive the fight.

npc.name: Tebo Reedwake
npc.description: A wiry human boatman who ferries legal cargo, illegal rumors, and anyone brave enough to sit still in a reed-skiff.
npc.dialogue: Do not smile with teeth at Hawga Daar. Teeth mean challenge unless you are eating. Sometimes both.

npc.name: Velis Orrenwater
npc.description: A soaked half-elf scholar who has been politely refused entry to Hawga Daar for eleven consecutive days.
npc.dialogue: They say Hawga Daar means Lost King. I believe the name is not metaphor. I also believe saying that too loudly will get me pushed into a bog.

npc.name: Thraax-of-the-Closed-Gate
npc.description: A broad-jawed lizardfolk watch speaker with painted warning marks across his throat scales.
npc.dialogue: Outsiders bring maps, then taxes, then graves. Stand where I see your hands.

npc.name: Ssharketh Brood-Mother
npc.description: The clan leader wears no crown, only bead strings naming every hatchling, hunter, and elder under her protection.
npc.dialogue: Trust is not spoken. Trust is carried in the mouth of the marsh and returned alive.

npc.name: Issra Warm-Nest
npc.description: A careful broodwarden who counts eggs, weather, strangers, and knives with equal seriousness.
npc.dialogue: Soft shells become hard scales if fools do not step on them first.

npc.name: Vhaak Mud-Spear
npc.description: A scarred lizardfolk hunter who smells blood in the reeds before insects find it.
npc.dialogue: You want clan trust? Hunt what hunts us. Bring back proof, not a story.

npc.name: Old-Scale Korr
npc.description: An elderly lizardfolk whose cataract-clouded eyes sharpen whenever old Draconic names are spoken.
npc.dialogue: Stone forgets slower than meat. Bring me a stone that remembers the Lost King.

npc.name: Nema Under-Moon
npc.description: A quiet shaman seated in a sunken royal doorway, reading ripples that move against the wind.
npc.dialogue: The crown below is not our crown. Still, it poisons our water because outsiders died clutching it.

npc.name: Drokh Valve-Biter
npc.description: A lizardfolk engineer with bronze tools, webbed gloves, and a personal grudge against ancient plumbing.
npc.dialogue: Old kings loved water until it entered their boots. Take this crank and teach the vaults humility.

npc.name: Raaksha Bone-Song
npc.description: A bonewright who carves hooks, charms, and spearheads while humming genealogies under her breath.
npc.dialogue: Bone is honest. It says what carried weight and what broke.

npc.name: Echo of Captain Ildran
npc.description: A fading human ghost with a rusted officer’s gorget and eyes finally emptied of command.
npc.dialogue: The crown was never ours to guard. We mistook possession for duty and drowned with the difference.

npc.name: The Poleman Without Ripples
npc.description: A translucent barge pilot whose pole never touches bottom and whose cargo manifest lists names instead of crates.
npc.dialogue: One name short. Always one name short. Pay the toll with memory, not coin.

npc.name: Mender Ssaali
npc.description: A small, copper-scaled healer who trusts plants more readily than people but does not confuse caution for cruelty.
npc.dialogue: Lotus heals fever. Listening heals insult. Outsiders usually bring both fever and insult.

npc.name: Yasira of the Starcloth
npc.description: A tall Ajuna woman wrapped in blue starcloth, Yasira treats mirages as geometry and politics as an irritating branch of weather prediction.

npc.name: Borun Brass-Eye
npc.description: A broad dwarf-descended nomad with brass lenses over one eye, Borun believes every mystery deserves a hinge, screw, and safety note.

npc.name: Naleth of the Quiet Bell
npc.description: A soft-spoken Shakni elder whose bells make no sound until a lie is spoken nearby.

npc.name: Roadmarshal Tavik Veilhand
npc.description: A scarred highway rider who knows every buried milestone and every place where a caravan can vanish in full sunlight.

npc.name: Saffi Three-Horizons
npc.description: A young Ajuna theorist who sketches spell diagrams in the air and erases them before rivals can copy the last line.

npc.name: Merek Sandledger
npc.description: A Dhanor accountant with an abacus of glass beads and an iron memory for missing crates, suspicious delays, and expensive excuses.

npc.name: Ishun Glassflute
npc.description: A musician-mage who tunes glass flutes to silence storms, angry camels, and occasionally shouting scholars.

npc.name: Thirana Pale-Compass
npc.description: A Silver Concord observer sent to determine whether the dead star has distorted Glasswind’s ancient mirror network.

npc.name: Omes of the Blue Pot
npc.description: A cheerful tea seller who hears more research gossip than any official envoy because everyone underestimates hot water.

npc.name: Luminous Aunt Veyra
npc.description: An elderly Ajuna aunt who sells formula scrolls only after correcting the buyer’s posture and pronunciation.

npc.name: Kherm Lenshook
npc.description: A precise merchant whose caravan carries lensbucklers, heat-thread repairs, spare axles, and small lectures about warranty limits.

npc.name: Silent Cousin Orresh
npc.description: A veiled notary who writes spells silently and taps the price on a sandclock before allowing negotiation.

npc.name: Edran Voss
npc.description: A frightened deserter who claims the Crownless Cabal wanted the Invisible Dungeon not for treasure, but for a workshop no army could find.

npc.name: Auralis in Blue Glass
npc.description: A recorded memory trapped in blue glass, repeating the last safe alignment of the Astral Crown’s mirage ward.

npc.name: Marra Lowtide
npc.description: A hard-eyed half-elf road guide with a salt-cracked cloak and a ledger of travelers who did not listen.
npc.dialogue: Terrecester is not a fishing village with walls. It is a harbor at war. Learn the bells before you follow the gulls.

npc.name: Harbormaster Veyla Terrecester
npc.description: A broad-shouldered human official who treats every dock plank as her jurisdiction and every hungry family as League business.
npc.dialogue: The League keeps the coast alive. Some call that control. I call it keeping pirate hooks out of children.

npc.name: Tibalt Quayreed
npc.description: A cheerful dock merchant with waterproof ledgers, gull feathers in his hat, and one eye always on the tide-clock.
npc.dialogue: If it floats, rusts, heals, cuts, or keeps rain out, I have a legal version and a cheaper version I never mentioned.

npc.name: Lira Netmender
npc.description: A young scout with a net needle, signal flags, and a habit of naming pirate ships after rude barnyard animals.
npc.dialogue: The raiders are not random. Kobold rafts drive us inward while human cutters mark the heavy cargo. Someone taught them our schedule.

npc.name: Tide-Echo of Eshdru
npc.description: A translucent echo shed from the ancient serpent’s memory, speaking in tide-slow sentences after the trial is complete.
npc.dialogue: The pearl was never hidden from the strong. It was hidden from the unready.

npc.name: Watch-Captain Marna Beld
npc.description: A scarred captain whose blue League sash has been mended with fishing line more than once.
npc.dialogue: Raiders hit supply carts, not glory patrols. That means they know what keeps the town standing.

npc.name: Gate-Sergeant Orrin Pell
npc.description: A square-jawed sergeant with salt in his beard and a voice made for making crowds step back.
npc.dialogue: If you bring trouble through my gate, at least bring it where I can see it.

npc.name: Commander Seressa Knifewake
npc.description: A tiefling naval commander with a hook-scar across one horn and a tactical map tattooed on her left forearm.
npc.dialogue: Privateers respect fear, pay, and weather. Today we have weather. Bring me the other two.

npc.name: Admiral Ysolde Nine-Tides
npc.description: An elderly dwarf admiral whose medals are dull with sea spray and whose eyes miss nothing near a shoreline.
npc.dialogue: The League survives because captains argue, vote, and still sail when the bell rings.

npc.name: Councilor Rul Terrecester
npc.description: A polished half-orc councilor descended from the wharf’s founders, careful with words and ruthless with contracts.
npc.dialogue: A free coast is not an ungoverned coast. Ask the pirates which one they prefer.

npc.name: Ticketmistress Pella Vane
npc.description: A halfling clerk behind brass bars, armed with ink, stamps, and an absolute refusal to bend ferry policy for heroic pleading.
npc.dialogue: One ticket, one stamped route, no exceptions. Hearthwatch sales are closed because roads are meant to be traveled in order.

npc.name: Captain Luro Brinehand
npc.description: A weather-bent gnome ferry captain whose left glove is always wet and whose boat bells ring even when still.
npc.dialogue: I can get you to Hearthwatch, to Glendes, or to regret. Two of those require a ticket.

npc.name: Sister Maevra of the Returning Tide
npc.description: A calm priest with mother-of-pearl prayer beads and a knife for cutting drowned ghosts free from wreckage.
npc.dialogue: The sea returns what it chooses. Our work is to be ready, grateful, and occasionally armed.

npc.name: Master Shipwright Anlo Tarhand
npc.description: A broad human shipwright whose hands are black with pitch and whose temper worsens around sabotage.
npc.dialogue: Cut a rope and you cut a life. Find who did it before I start testing knots on suspects.

npc.name: Hellis Vowglass
npc.description: A Silver Concord mage seconded to the drydock, studying tide-glass wards with the expression of someone who misses quiet libraries.
npc.dialogue: A ship ward is a spell that has agreed to get wet. Mine have been tampered with.

npc.name: Widow Elane Codds
npc.description: A fisher widow who mends nets for half the town and remembers every sailor by the knot they tied.
npc.dialogue: A missing net can tell you more than a shouting sailor. Mine was cut, not torn.

npc.name: Mother Sennit
npc.description: A round, severe cook who feeds refugees, sailors, orphans, and informants from the same steaming cauldron.
npc.dialogue: Hungry people talk. Full people tell the truth slower, but with better details.

npc.name: Auditor Jem Lockwater
npc.description: A meticulous auditor with wax seals dangling from every pocket and a smile like a closed ledger.
npc.dialogue: False warrants are worse than forged coin. Coin steals goods. Warrants steal authority.

npc.name: Nadin Blue-Veil
npc.description: A Blue Veil trader who moves salt, glass, rumors, and magical reagents between Glasswind and the coast.
npc.dialogue: The sea has markets the desert understands: scarcity, mirage, and men who swear their map is honest.

npc.name: Vannis Shell-Eye
npc.description: A nervous scholar wearing shell spectacles and carrying rubbings of every wall except the one that nearly ate him.
npc.dialogue: The Buried Labyrinth is not a tomb. It is a test that grew teeth.

npc.name: Rikrik No-Flag
npc.description: A soaked kobold privateer deserter clutching a white shell like a surrender flag.
npc.dialogue: No more boom-boats. No more captains who count kobolds as fuses. Rikrik wants shore-law now.

npc.name: Rellan Cloudmark
npc.description: A weather-burned guide with copper beads braided into his beard to warn him before lightning strikes nearby stone.
npc.dialogue: The path up is not hard because it climbs. It is hard because the mountain asks why you climb.

npc.name: Matriarch Ysbet Wind-Latch
npc.description: The elected matriarch of Shepherd’s Eyrie, keeper of storm-season ledgers, herd rights, and old agreements with the giants.
npc.dialogue: Help my people breathe through this storm, then I will help you speak where thunder listens.

npc.name: Brannik Weatherwise
npc.description: A compact merchant whose packs are organized by altitude, wind direction, and how close the buyer looks to panic.
npc.dialogue: Buy rope before prophecy. One saves you more often.

npc.name: Ilyra Far-Ridge
npc.description: A Marchwarden scout posted to the upper switchback to track Cabal sappers, missing climbers, and unnatural lightning strikes.
npc.dialogue: The raiders are not trying to hold the bridge. They are trying to make the bridge angry.

npc.name: Echo of Foreman Dagna
npc.description: The freed echo of a Dawnhammer dwarf miner whose bones were dragged into the storm engine and forced to work after death.
npc.dialogue: Break his circle. Then take the Aegis as a shield, not a crown.

npc.name: Mina Bellherd
npc.description: A teenage goat-herder with a sling, a weather eye, and no patience for travelers who underestimate livestock.
npc.dialogue: A goat knows a bad storm before a wizard has finished naming it.

npc.name: Old Nessa Highroof
npc.description: An elder who keeps meal rotations, guest lists, and storm-shelter rules with terrifying precision.
npc.dialogue: No one freezes in my common while I have soup or opinions.

npc.name: Senn the Ropewalker
npc.description: A ropewalker who crosses cliff-lines carrying medicine, gossip, and the occasional terrified outsider.
npc.dialogue: Do not look down unless down has information you need.

npc.name: Toma of the Struck Chimney
npc.description: A patient innkeeper who marks each lightning strike on the chimney and each foolish climber on the wall behind the bar.
npc.dialogue: Tea first. Heroics after your hands stop shaking.

npc.name: Savi Cloudless
npc.description: A Blue Veil peddler collecting high-altitude charms and selling desert lenscloth to people who have never seen a dune.
npc.dialogue: The desert and the peak agree on one thing: weather is a language.

npc.name: Elaun Sky-Kneeler
npc.description: A cliff-priest who blesses climbing lines, buries lightning victims, and translates thunder into practical warnings.
npc.dialogue: Thunder is not anger. Anger is much less patient.

npc.name: Rusk Feather-Covenant
npc.description: A scarred keeper responsible for maintaining the old treaty between Shepherd’s Eyrie and the wild griffons above the roost.
npc.dialogue: We do not own them. We ask, and we pay in respect.

npc.name: Envoy Caldus Vey
npc.description: A cold-fingered envoy comparing the dead-star readings from Glasswind with the prophetic weather records of Vhal Torunn.
npc.dialogue: The relics no longer need to share names to share a pattern.

npc.name: Maelthra Storm-Vow
npc.description: A storm giant guardian in dark blue mail, suspicious of every small folk kingdom, faction, oath, and emergency.
npc.dialogue: Small hands broke the old seals once. Prove yours can mend before they ask to carry.

npc.name: Jorund Sky-Hearer
npc.description: An ancient storm giant oracle whose beard is braided with rainstones. He listens to thunder as if it is a courtroom record.
npc.dialogue: The dead star is not above us. It is behind the laws that keep above and below apart.

npc.name: Orvanth Cloud-Smith
npc.description: A patient cloud-smith with hands large enough to crush a wagon and precise enough to repair a mortal buckle.
npc.dialogue: Bring me what the raiders stole, and I will make the Stormlift remember mercy.

npc.name: Kell of the Small Anvil
npc.description: A mortal apprentice to Orvanth who sells sanctioned storm formulae in script small enough for ordinary spellbooks.
npc.dialogue: No refunds for spells cast during hail. That is in the first line.

npc.name: Keeper Veyra Lift-Bound
npc.description: A giant-taught human keeper who maintains the Stormlift base and refuses to let panic override ascent law.
npc.dialogue: The lift rises for proof, not impatience.

npc.name: Sarro of the Rain Court
npc.description: A silent attendant who records rain color, wind taste, and the exact number of lies told under each storm.
npc.dialogue: Blue rain means grief. Silver rain means judgment. Black rain means run.

npc.name: Shale of the Blackfall
npc.description: A scarred deep gnome climber wrapped in glowmoss rope and old surface medals. He measures newcomers by how they treat borrowed light.
npc.dialogue: Do not ask how far down. Ask what you are willing to leave above.

npc.name: Vessa Lanternwarden
npc.description: A blind human warden whose staff is hung with tiny light-crystals, each one owed to someone dead or saved.
npc.dialogue: You want entry? Bring back stolen light. Down here, trust begins with what you refuse to waste.

npc.name: Mother Velvetcap
npc.description: A broad-hatted myconid elder who communicates through spores, slate taps, and a patient translator.
npc.dialogue: The surface speaks of kingdoms. The Depths ask a simpler question: did you poison the water?

npc.name: Ikxit Blue-Wick
npc.description: A precise kobold with blue candle stubs tied along his tail and a ledger of every flame lent to strangers.
npc.dialogue: Two drops oil, one pinch wick-salt, no shouting near the nursery caps. Rules keep softskins edible less often.

npc.name: Nimri Three-Down
npc.description: A deep gnome mapmaker who temporarily forgot which way was up and now distrusts all arrows.
npc.dialogue: Maps are lies agreed upon by people who have not fallen through the floor yet.

npc.name: Maav of the Quiet Bloom
npc.description: A myconid interpreter whose cap blooms with pale symbols whenever the Choir recalls a dead traveler.
npc.dialogue: We do not forget. We compost. There is a difference.

npc.name: Borvak Freehammer
npc.description: A duergar smith who broke his own taskmaster brand and now refuses all chains, including polite ones.
npc.dialogue: A hammer can make a shackle or crack one. I decided which sound I prefer.

npc.name: Seryne Nocturne
npc.description: A drow astronomer who studies the dead star by reconstructing a sky she can no longer see.
npc.dialogue: Do not confuse darkness with ignorance. The surface has sunlight and still misses the obvious.

npc.name: Elian Lastsong
npc.description: An elderly descendant of a lost surface expedition, preserving sky-memory through inherited songs.
npc.dialogue: My grandmother never saw dawn. She taught me the song anyway.

npc.name: Tholm Ashenhand
npc.description: A soot-fingered broker who knows which debts are honest, which are poisonous, and which smell like the Cabal.
npc.dialogue: Bone, crystal, silence, maps. Someone is buying ingredients for a very bad idea.

npc.name: Ayra Below-Rain
npc.description: A calm woman with silvered eyes who listens to underground water as if it were testimony.
npc.dialogue: This pool has begun speaking dead kings’ names. Water should remember stone, not crowns.

npc.name: Vond Without-Collar
npc.description: A bruised duergar refugee hiding near Cabal chains, terrified of capture and furious at his own fear.
npc.dialogue: If you came to save us, stop talking like a banner and start cutting iron.

npc.name: Suul of the Mycelial Choir
npc.description: A small, luminous myconid node grown from preserved warnings of people who died carrying maps.
npc.dialogue: The old roads are written in spores. Breathe gently, or you will read too much.

npc.name: Keth Blackwater
npc.description: A wiry keeper with a spear, a bucket, and no patience for anyone who fouls the Compact’s water.
npc.dialogue: Light can be traded. Food can be grown. Bad water kills everyone equally.

npc.name: Orrix Debtknife
npc.description: A sharp-eyed judge who settles disputes in iron tokens, memory beads, and occasionally blood.
npc.dialogue: Every debt is a tunnel. Choose where it opens before you crawl in.

npc.name: Echo of the Buried Sun
npc.description: A warm outline of a long-dead Concord keeper, preserved in the only honest light inside the ossuary.
npc.dialogue: The Sun-Mote is not a weapon. It is proof that the dark has boundaries.

npc.name: Witness Beneath Nightscale
npc.description: A masked Compact envoy sent to witness whether the player frees, kills, binds, or bargains with the Umbralwyrm.
npc.dialogue: The Compact does not require mercy. It requires that you understand the cost of your choice.

npc.name: Vena Brokenchain
npc.description: A scarred human commander chosen by the escaped prisoners because she refuses crowns, ranks, and despair.
npc.dialogue: No one here was supposed to survive. That makes every breath a rebellion.

npc.name: Mother Liska Apple-End
npc.description: A halfling cook from Greenbarrow who has turned three stolen cauldrons into the Refuge’s morale engine.
npc.dialogue: Eat. Then panic if you must. Empty stomachs serve the Cabal.

npc.name: Threx Siltprayer
npc.description: A lizardfolk healer taken from Hawga Daar and now tending wounds in a half-flooded reliquary.
npc.dialogue: Softskins waste blood by letting it leave the body. Hold still.

npc.name: Sable of Unreturned Names
npc.description: A fey envoy who escaped a name-vault with half a title and all of her anger intact.
npc.dialogue: The Citadel steals names before it steals bodies. That is how it makes obedience sound natural.

npc.name: Borun Chainforge
npc.description: A dwarven forge-prison survivor who repairs armor while reciting the names of captured smiths.
npc.dialogue: Forced work is not craft. It is a wound wearing an apron.

npc.name: Yasira Last-Lens
npc.description: A Blue Veil researcher whose mirage diagrams now map a fortress trying to become real.
npc.dialogue: The Citadel has direction, but no right to arrive.

npc.name: Korun of the Broken Fulmen
npc.description: A wounded giant-servitor carrying a storm rune larger than a shield.
npc.dialogue: The high ones judged slowly. The Lich broke quickly. We must mend faster than both.

npc.name: Sister Marivane of the Open Door
npc.description: A Concord cleric who now blesses people she may never see leave.
npc.dialogue: Hope is not confidence. Hope is choosing the next useful mercy.

npc.name: Dhani of the Last Equation
npc.description: A sand-burned spellwright selling formulas copied while the walls were rearranging themselves.
npc.dialogue: Prices are high because time is short and ink keeps evaporating.

npc.name: Quartermaster Pell of No Banner
npc.description: A former Cabal wagon clerk who defected when he realized ledgers could become chains.
npc.dialogue: I know what they stole because I wrote it down. Now I write down what we take back.

npc.name: The Crown Witness
npc.description: A silent figure wrapped in prison cloth, speaking only when the final throne is near. No one agrees which race they are.
npc.dialogue: The Crown was never lost. It was waiting to see who would mistake possession for worthiness.
